title: Grove outsources its day-to-day execution to a separate Executor Agent, Amatsu, through the Executor Accord Primitive
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.2.1 records an **Active** Executor Accord Primitive for Grove with a single live Instance named Amatsu (A.6.1.1.2.2.2.1.2.1). Its parameters section A.6.1.1.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1 does not define the roles inline; it points outward: "The Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps for Amatsu are specified in [A.6.1.2.1 - Operational Executor Agent Amatsu]."

That indirection is the architecture. Grove, a Prime Agent, does not staff its own execution functions — it enters an Accord with a purpose-built **Executor Agent** whose own Artifact holds the role assignments. Grove's Artifact specifies *that* execution is delegated and under what process; Amatsu's specifies *who* executes.

The separation lets one Executor Agent serve multiple Primes with a shared operational apparatus, and lets Grove change executors by opening a new Accord Instance rather than rewriting its own governance. Because the Executor Accord is an Operational Primitive rather than a Genesis Primitive, it remains re-invocable — the delegation is intentionally reversible.

The corresponding exposure is that Grove's day-to-day integrity depends on a document it does not control. A change to Amatsu's Artifact changes who can act for Grove, so Grove's risk surface extends into another Agent's governance.
description: Amatsu supplies Grove's Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps roles, so a Prime Agent's operational authority is defined in another Agent's Artifact rather than its own.
